A Public Address on the Memorial Day of Master Fojian Last year, on this very day, the clay oxen fought their way into the sea. Today, on this very day, the stone women ascend the mountain. If you can see it here, you will see that the Buddhas and patriarchs have never been hidden; if you cannot see it here, you will not avoid being lost in the weeds. In the past, when the World-Honored One was about to enter nirvana, he addressed the assembly, saying: "All conditioned things are impermanent; how can one not feel sorrow? At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, weeping, said to the Buddha: "The World-Honored One has already attained the ultimate Way; why do you still speak of sorrow? The Buddha replied: "Ānanda, you have served me for twenty years, yet you have never once asked me what the ultimate meaning is. This is why, today, on this memorial day, I address the assembly: If you can see through the words of the Buddhas and patriarchs, you will see that the clay oxen have long since entered the sea and the stone women have ascended the mountain. If you can see it thus, you will know that the Buddhas and patriarchs have never been hidden; if you cannot see it thus, you will remain lost in the weeds. Therefore, I ask you all: Where is the place where the Buddhas and patriarchs are not hidden? Speak! Speak! *Note: This text is a memorial address (jichun shizhong) given by a master on the anniversary of the passing of his predecessor, Master Fojian.*
